title: Staged release curation and recovery framework
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: Implement a composable framework to define staged model introductions with deterministic split control, shadow probing, conservative promotion schedules, and automated recovery (soft-fail rollback + quarantine). This is intended to give teams a single declarative config they can attach to routes or model families to manage multi-step exposure and safe degradation paths.

Background: We currently have ad-hoc rollout behavior implemented in several places: temporary traffic splits in the console, manual shadowing via integrations, and separate alert-driven runbooks. That leads to inconsistent safety margins across teams and a lot of manual operational toil when a new model shows regressions. The goal is to centralize the policy primitives and provide a reusable engine that can be composed into Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes.

Goals: 
- Provide a declarative rollout schema covering traffic fractions, cohort targeting, step durations, and probe traffic.
- Support shadow probing (sampled traffic mirrored to candidate model) with independent success criteria.
- Evaluate simple metric predicates (latency, error rate, perplexity/quality score) and composite rules for auto-advance and auto-rollback.
- Expose hooks for manual hold, fast-forward, and forced rollback.
- Emit telemetry suitable for SLO guardrails and incident diagnosis.

Non-goals: 
- Full experimentation/bandit platform (only A/B through deterministic splits).
- Heavy-weight ML validation pipelines (we rely on existing eval infra to surface quality signals).

Design overview:
1) Policy manifest: a small JSON/YAML schema teams attach to a route or model version. Key primitives: steps (fraction, duration), probe (shadow sample rate and validation metrics), risk windows (warmup cooldown), rollback predicates (thresholds and hysteresis), and fallback variants (compatible smaller models or older versions).

2) Execution engine: controller that materializes traffic allocations in the serving control-plane and schedules step transitions. It listens to metrics stream (console telemetry) and evaluates predicates against sliding windows. If predicate violates, it will: (a) optionally quarantine candidate model to shadow-only; (b) initiate rollback to previous stable variant; (c) notify owners and create an incident stub.

3) Probe subsystem: lightweight mirror path that attaches to existing routing layer without affecting primary latency path. Probe responses go to an isolated evaluator that computes mismatch rates against baseline and aggregates quality signals.

4) Observability and playbooks: per-policy dashboards, per-step events, and a small set of canned runbook actions (hold, step-back, full rollback).

Configuration example (illustrative):
---
apiVersion: rollout.redwood/v1
kind: StagedRelease
metadata:
  name: rtx-2026-03-small-model-test
spec:
  targetRoute: /completions/summary
  candidateModel: rtx-small:2026-03-08
  baselineModel: rtx-large:stable
  steps:
    - fraction: 0.01
      duration: 30m
    - fraction: 0.10
      duration: 2h
    - fraction: 0.50
      duration: 6h
    - fraction: 1.00
      duration: 24h
  shadowProbe:
    sampleRate: 0.02
    validators:
      - name: latency
        threshold_ms: 250
      - name: exact-match-delta
        metric: nll_delta
        threshold: 0.12
  rollbackPredicates:
    - name: latency-spike
      metric: p95_latency_ms
      window: 5m
      threshold: 400
      hysteresis: 2m
    - name: quality-regression
      metric: nll_delta
      window: 30m
      threshold: 0.15
      occurrences: 3
  fallback: ["rtx-small:canary-slim","rtx-large:stable"]
  notifyOn: ["owner","platform-sre"]
---

Compatibility notes: The engine will initially run in Hosted control plane; Dedicated clusters will use a lighter control loop that emits desired allocations which an allocator applies locally. Private deployments can opt-in to run the controller if they expose metrics to the control plane; otherwise, the controller can operate in a dry-run advisory mode.

Migration plan:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement manifest parser, step scheduler, and minimal allocation applier for Hosted. Build dashboard in console for per-policy state.
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): shadow probe subsystem and predicate evaluator; add auto-rollback actions.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): Dedicated integration + RBAC for policy ownership and audit logs.

Success criteria:
- Policy applied to internal pilot routes reduces manual rollback toil by 50% (measured by SRE incident annotations).
- No customer-facing latency impact from probe subsystem (shadow sample path stays <1% of primary CPU budget).
- Rollbacks executed automatically with correct predicate detection in at least 3/3 internal simulated regressions.

Constraints & open questions:
- Predicate expressivity vs safety: we prefer conservative, few-operator predicates at launch. We will explore richer DSL only after initial adoption.
- Cross-region rollout semantics: should we allow stagger by region? Proposed: yes as optional field.

Security & compliance: audit trails for rollout changes, signed manifests for Private deployments, and KMS integration for sensitive notification endpoints.

Operational notes: integrate with existing runbooks in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Release+Curator. Track PRs in GH under rdx/release-curator.
